correctness.rationale: The feasible part masses t_i lie in the rank-two hypersimplex; choosing an edge between a pair of parts with those pair marginals and choosing its endpoints from the normalized within-part weights recovers the given feasible vector. Strict feasibility uses t_i=2/k distributed positively within each part; the frozen proof's stray suggestion x_v=2/n is not valid for unbalanced sizes, but its immediately following strictly feasible construction is. After deletion of one or two vertices every part survives, so coordinate facets and their pair intersections have the stated dimensions, by the same strict feasibility in remaining coordinates. A part-cap face is a product of two simplices, and one coordinate deletion lowers its dimension by one; two caps force all mass into those parts, dropping dimension to at most n−5. Each ridge belongs to exactly two facets (its pointed two-dimensional normal cone). Within the sum-zero direction space, c_v=−e_v+1/n and d_i=1_{A_i}−a_i/n (constant vectors implicit) give squared norms (n−1)/n and a_i(n−a_i)/n. The coordinate cross term is −1/n and the coordinate–cap cross terms are −(n−a_i)/n inside and a_i/n outside. Taking the supplement of the projected normal angle gives precisely both signs, the multiplicities and the split adjacency graph. The two cap families are strictly increasing in a_i at fixed n and lie on opposite sides of π/2; equality of the acute cap angle with the coordinate angle requires a_i=n−1, excluded here. An independent rational affine-rank and signed Gram test passed profiles (3,3,3), (3,3,4), (3,4,5) and (3,3,3,3).
residual_risks: Uniform coordinate mass is not used as a proof step; use the correct second construction in the record. Finite checks only corroborate the dimension and rational cosine calculations. No assertion for parts of size one or two, or for a metric other than the stated intrinsic Euclidean one.

evidence: Complete multipartite edge polytopes are canonical loopless rank-two matroid base polytopes with the equivalence an equality in vertex coordinates. The Resultary result in this exact realization gives Gaussian exposure probabilities of vertices. The stable-set result instead has adjacency among facets of the hull of stable-set indicator vectors.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A Gaussian probability of selecting a vertex measures the solid angle of its full normal cone, not the aperture of a two-facet ridge normal cone. The stable-set hull, which includes the origin and each single-vertex indicator, is not the edge hull in sum=2. Neither is an equivalent formulation of the metric invariant under review.

value.rationale: The full interior dihedral spectrum is a natural intrinsic metric invariant of canonical rank-two base polytopes, not merely the f-vector in different notation. Its exact classification distinguishes uniformity of the coarse acute/obtuse data from monotone dependence on class sizes of every genuinely metric cap-angle family. The full multiplicities and noncollision property matter for comparing the Euclidean geometry of polytopes with the same facet-adjacency graph; the value does not rest on the already-known number of ridges or on any single routine angle computation.
residual_risks: No assertion about small parts, higher-codimension angular spectra, or weighted ridge measures.
